findings.title: attestation_signers get notes.attacher but no permission to sign with the attestor's KMS key
findings.explanation: The attestor only accepts attestations signed by the KMS key version registered on it, and the variable promises signers 'can create attestations', but the module grants them only roles/containeranalysis.notes.attacher. Without cloudkms signerVerifier on the key the CI identity cannot sign, so no image can be attested and the ENFORCED_BLOCK default rule blocks every deployment. Principle is a best fit: the policy works, the delivery pipeline it depends on cannot.
findings.remediation: Grant each attestation signer roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier on var.signing_key_id, and document the project-level roles/containeranalysis.occurrences.editor they also need.

findings.title: Attestor trusts a single signing key version, so a key rotation instantly invalidates every existing attestation
findings.explanation: public_keys is built from one data.google_kms_crypto_key_version. The example's own comment says to rotate by adding a key version and registering it on the attestor, but changing signing_key_version replaces the only public key, so every running image attested with the old version is denied on its next reschedule until it is re-attested.
findings.remediation: Register a public key per trusted version: add var.additional_signing_key_versions and build public_keys with a dynamic block over a for_each data source.
